title: Vector Consumption: Packaging, SLAs, and Pricing PRD
author: Priya Raman
content:
Executive summary:

This PRD defines a packaged commercial offering for Redwood's Vector Consumption Service (VCS) that covers packaging tiers, operational SLAs, telemetry requirements, and a pragmatic pricing model to support lightweight developer usage through enterprise contracts. The product objective is to provide predictable cost and performance for vector creation, storage, and similarity queries while enabling enterprise controls (KMS, VPC) and clear migration paths for existing customers.

Scope and audience:
- Product, pricing, and GTM teams for commercialization decisions.
- Engineering teams: eng-serving-runtime, eng-platform, eng-developer-experience.
- Finance, Legal, and Security for contract and compliance work.

Key goals:
- Deliver three clear packages: Sandbox, Standard, and Enterprise with distinct throughput, retention, and SLA characteristics.
- Instrument metering to separate compute (query) and storage (hot/cold) billing signals, and enable volume discounts and reserved capacity.
- Provide operational SLOs and an incident credit mechanism that is simple to calculate and auditable.

Packages overview:
1) Sandbox (developer-focused)
   - Target: prototyping and low-volume apps.
   - Throughput: up to 25k embeddings/month; burst-friendly but rate-limited.
   - Retention: default 7 days; upgradeable to 30 days for small fee.
   - SLA: best-effort; no financial credits.
   - Billing: per-embedding unit; small storage fee.

2) Standard (self-serve paid)
   - Target: production SaaS and mid-market customers.
   - Throughput: up to 2M embeddings/day or 250 embeddings/sec sustained; credit pool for bursts.
   - Retention: 30/90 day options; hot and cold storage tiers.
   - SLA: 99.9% monthly availability across ingest and query endpoints; latency targets apply to vectors up to 1536 dims.
   - Billing: per-embedding with volume tiers, separate storage and optional query compute metering.

3) Enterprise (contracted)
   - Target: regulated enterprises and platform teams.
   - Throughput: reserved capacity with contractual QPS and warm-pool guarantees.
   - Retention: configurable (30/90/365+), VPC or on-prem archival options.
   - SLA: 99.95% availability; custom latency guarantees by agreement.
   - Billing: committed monthly fee + overage; optional KMS/HSM and dedicated support add-ons.

Operational SLOs and credit policy:
- Standard SLOs:
  - Availability: 99.9% monthly for API surface (ingest/query).
  - Latency: 95th percentile query latency <= 150ms for vectors <=1536 dims; 99th <= 400ms.
- Enterprise SLOs: availability 99.95%; 95th percentile latency <= 100ms (negotiable).
- Credit policy (simplified): monthly_credit = monthly_invoice * max(0, (SLO_target - measured_availability) / SLO_target). Exact legal phrasing to be produced by Legal.

Telemetry and alerts:
- Mandatory tenant metrics: ingest_rate, query_rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, error_rate, storage_bytes_hot, storage_bytes_cold, retention_evictions.
- Alerts to page: sustained error_rate >0.5% for 5 minutes, p95 latency >2x target for 5 minutes, retention_eviction_spike > configured threshold.
- Dashboards: per-tenant usage, estimated monthly cost, retention forecast, and anomaly detection panel.

Functional requirements (FRs):
- FR1: Public API for single and batch operations: upsert_vector, delete_vector, bulk_upsert, vector_search, and export_vectors. Each request supports idempotency keys.
- FR2: Tenant retention policy controls exposed via Console and API with export-on-demand (NDJSON).
- FR3: RBAC for project/team scoping; API keys and scoped tokens; Enterprise support for BYOK and per-tenant KMS integration.
- FR4: Billing events emitted per action with dimensions: tenant_id, action_type, vector_dimensions_billed, storage_tier.
- FR5: Burst credit system for Standard; reserved capacity allocator for Enterprise with warm-pool preallocation.

Non-functional requirements (NFRs):
- NFR1: Support end-to-end multi-region failover for Enterprise with max failover time 60s for control-plane routing.
- NFR2: Index durability: hot replication 3x and cold tier snapshot cadence 24h with immutable snapshots.
- NFR3: Deletion assurance: soft-delete immediate, permanent purge within 24h (Sandbox), 6h (Standard), 2h (Enterprise).
- NFR4: Performance: platform should handle staging load >50k vectors/sec ingest for scale tests.

Pricing model (principles):
- Separate storage and compute to make cost drivers transparent.
- Per-embedding unit applies to storage and initial ingest compute. Vectors are normalized into 1k-dim blocks for billing: bill_units = ceil(dimensions / 1024).
- Offer volume discounts and committed throughput discounts to encourage committed revenue.

Example pricing tables (illustrative):
- Sandbox: $0.0007 per embedding unit; $0.12 / GB-month hot storage.
- Standard: $0.0004 per embedding unit (baseline), discounts at 50M+ embeddings/month. Storage $0.07 / GB-month (hot). Reserved throughput add-on $1500/month per 250 QPS.
- Enterprise: Custom: example $20k/month commitment for 8M embeddings + $0.00018 overage per embedding; KMS/HSM add-on $1k/mo + per-request fee.

Billing examples (simplified):
- Example 1: prototype with 40k embeddings/month on Sandbox -> 40k * $0.0007 = $28/month + storage.
- Example 2: Standard customer at 25M embeddings/month -> blended pricing depending on tiers; estimated monthly $6k-$8k excluding storage and reserved throughput.

API reference snippets (pseudo-code using single quotes for clarity):
- Bulk upsert example:
  POST /v1/vectors/bulk_upsert
  Body: '{
    'tenant_id': 'acme-42',
    'vectors': [
      {'id': 'doc-1', 'vector': [0.12, -0.03, ...], 'meta': {'source': 'kb'}},
      {'id': 'doc-2', 'vector': [0.02, 0.08, ...], 'meta': {'source': 'kb'}}
    ],
    'idempotency_key': 'bulk-202706-0001'
  }'

- Search example:
  POST /v1/vectors/search
  Body: '{
    'tenant_id': 'acme-42',
    'query_vector': [0.11, -0.02, ...],
    'top_k': 10,
    'filter': {'meta.source': 'kb'}
  }'

Security and compliance:
- Default encryption at rest and in transit. Enterprise: BYOK via customer-managed KMS, HSM support for key storage.
- Data residency: Region-scoped retention options for Enterprise; audit logging retained 365 days for Enterprise, 30 days for Standard.
- DSR/Deletion flows documented and automatable via API; include audit trail for compliance reviews.

Rollout plan and timeline:
- Phase 0 (Q3 2027): internal alpha for Sandbox; measure ingest/query latencies and surface dev console controls.
- Phase 1 (Q4 2027): public Beta for Standard; enable billing pipeline and per-tenant telemetry; invite 20 pilot customers.
- Phase 2 (Q1 2028): Enterprise GA with contractual SLAs, BYOK, VPC and legal templates.

Migration and customer onboarding:
- Provide an export/import tool that supports NDJSON vector dumps and an incremental bulk_upsert client with resume support.
- Offer a 60-90 day dual-write period and pre-migration performance validation for high-touch accounts.
- CS onboarding checklist: account sizing, retention recommendation, cost projection, 7-day staging soak test.

Dependencies and ownership:
- Serving runtime: ingestion pipeline, indexing, eviction logic (owner: eng-serving-runtime).
- Billing events and invoices: eng-platform and finance (owner: finance-and-legal + eng-platform).
- Console UI and API surface: eng-developer-experience.
- Security/KMS integration: security-and-compliance.

Open items and decision log:
- Decision required: whether query compute metering is default or opt-in for Standard.
- Decision required: exact billing normalization (512 vs 1024 dim bucket). Recommend 1024 for simplicity; finance to confirm.

Acceptance criteria for GA:
- End-to-end billing for 1k tenants with synthetic load validated.
- SLA telemetry and credit calc automated and reviewed by Legal/Finance.
- Console controls for retention and export available to tenants.
- BYOK and VPC config flows validated for at least one Enterprise pilot.

Appendix:
- Draft SLA clause and example credit calculation.
